prompt: How many real zeros does $p(x) = (x - 1)(x - 4)(x + 3)$ have?
hint: Each factor hides one zero. Count the factors.

hints.text: Each factor hides one zero. Count the factors.
The zeros are $x = 1$, $x = 4$, and $x = -3$ — all different.

explanation: Set each factor equal to zero one at a time.
That is $3$ different zeros, so the graph crosses the $x$-axis 3 times.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture the crossings
steps: Imagine a wiggly track drawn across a number line.
It dives through the axis at $-3$, then at 1, then at 4.
Three dives means three real zeros.
